recent_posts.title: Common pitfalls when building generative AI applications
recent_posts.summary: Common pitfalls in building generative AI applications include using AI unnecessarily, confusing poor product design with bad AI, starting with overly complex solutions, overestimating early success, relying solely on AI for evaluation, and lacking a strategy for use case selection. Focus on practical applications, user experience, validated evaluation methods, and strategic planning to avoid these errors.

recent_posts.title: Agents
recent_posts.summary: Intelligent agents are designed to perceive and act upon their environment, revolutionizing AI with applications ranging from data gathering and market research to website creation and customer account management. Key components involve tools and planning, with the ability to integrate various functions like web searching, SQL query execution, and automated data entry. Evaluating these agents includes assessing their planning abilities and addressing potential failure modes. Enhancing agent performance can involve tool augmentation and more sophisticated planning frameworks.

recent_posts.title: Collecting user feedback for generative AI applications
recent_posts.summary: User feedback is essential for evaluating and developing AI applications, especially those with conversational interfaces like chatbots and assistants. Effective user feedback collection systems can personalize models, improve future iterations, and maintain a competitive edge. The post discusses various types of feedback, including explicit and implicit feedback, and offers insights into designing non-intrusive feedback mechanisms. Additionally, it emphasizes the importance of respecting user privacy and understanding the biases inherent in user feedback to avoid degenerate feedback loops.

recent_posts.title: Building A Generative AI Platform
recent_posts.summary: The post details the construction of a generative AI platform, highlighting the common components such as context enhancement, guardrails, model routers, gateways, and caching techniques. It explores the complexities of context construction through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the necessity of guardrails for input and output protection. The article also discusses the importance of adding routers and gateways for handling multiple models, optimizing for cost and latency, and ensuring security. Observability and orchestration principles for managing extensive AI application flows are also covered.

recent_posts.title: Measuring personal growth
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses different metrics for measuring personal growth, including rate of change, time to solve problems, and number of future options. It explores the idea of treating oneself as an investment and the importance of becoming a new person every few years. The post also emphasizes the value of solving big problems and maximizing future options.

recent_posts.summary: Analysis of 900 popular open source AI tools, including the AI stack, data, model development, applications, infrastructure, open source AI developers, and the growing China's open source ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: Predictive Human Preference: From Model Ranking to Model Routing
recent_posts.summary: Human preference is a crucial tool for AI model development and can be used for model ranking and model routing. Predictive human preference can help improve response quality, reduce costs, and provide insights into a model's strengths and weaknesses. The preference predictor has an accuracy of 75-76.2% in non-tie matches.

recent_posts.title: Sampling for Text Generation
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses the sampling strategies used in text generation, including temperature, top-k, and top-p sampling. It covers the impact of these strategies on the model's creativity and coherence. The post also explores how to improve a model's performance through test time sampling and generate structured outputs in a desired format. Overall, understanding sampling techniques is crucial for leveraging AI models effectively.

recent_posts.title: Multimodality and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs)
recent_posts.summary: Multimodal systems involve working with multiple data modalities such as text, image, audio, and more. OpenAI's CLIP and DeepMind's Flamingo are significant models in the field. Flamingo extends CLIP by incorporating a language model component. Research directions in the field include incorporating more data modalities, developing multimodal systems for instruction-following, and creating adapters for more efficient multimodal training.

recent_posts.title: Open challenges in LLM research
recent_posts.summary: The article discusses open challenges in LLM research, including reducing hallucinations, optimizing context length and construction, incorporating other data modalities, improving model efficiency, designing new model architectures, developing GPU alternatives, making agents usable, improving learning from human preference, enhancing the chat interface, and building LLMs for non-English languages.
